purpose: A user can play both documented modes (A classic, B versus) of the Duel Blocks game end to end as described in app/README.md.

baseline.note: No prior stable release exists beyond this previous candidate; baseline behavior evidence taken from cand-good discover journeys J1-J4 and its evidence transcripts. baseline: previous-candidate (single).

identity_verification.note: README sha256 is identical to the cand-good round (docs unchanged between candidates), so mode-behavior deltas cannot be explained by documentation changes.

differences.delta: Mode B lost all three sound-effect markers that existed in the previous candidate: [sound:lock.wav] after move 4, [sound:clear.wav] after move 5, and [sound:attack.wav] after move 6 are all absent in cand-bad; only [fx:screen-shake] survives.
differences.evidence: Baseline .opencode/mvp/observation/G-OBS/cand-good/evidence/mode-b-run1.txt shows all four markers; live rerun .opencode/mvp/observation/G-OBS/cand-bad/evidence/c1-modeb-20260921-004446.txt shows only [fx:screen-shake]. Deterministic (identical result in discover captures j2-modeb-noinput/j2-modeb-repro2 and the fresh live probe).
differences.expected_basis: app/README.md (unchanged sha256 across both candidates): 'Both modes feature block-lock and line-clear sound effects; mode B additionally plays attack sound effects and a screen-shake flash on line clears.' Regression is real product damage, not a doc change; discover finding F-002 is thereby classified as a regression introduced between cand-good and cand-bad, not a never-worked feature.

differences.delta: Consequence of D-1: mode B's transcript now differs from mode A's only by the single [fx:screen-shake] marker (scores identical, 1200). In the baseline, mode B was distinguishable from mode A by attack sound plus screen-shake; the versus experience has become almost indistinguishable from single-player.
differences.evidence: Diff of .opencode/mvp/observation/G-OBS/cand-bad/evidence/c1-modea-20260921-004446.txt vs c1-modeb-20260921-004446.txt: exactly one differing line ([fx:screen-shake]).

differences.delta: None. Mode A's undocumented 'move 6: attack' (no target, no sound) is present identically in baseline and current candidate; baseline discover had already recorded it as its F-001 (medium, continuity).
differences.expected_basis: Present in baseline evidence mode-a-run1.txt; not introduced by this candidate. Per local rules this does not dismiss the finding; it remains open at medium severity.
differences.note: Owner may classify attack-in-mode-A as intended flavor; until then it stays a known-old issue.

differences.delta: None. Full non-interactivity (fixed self-playing 6-move script, stdin ignored, instant 'game over: score 1200') existed identically in the baseline (cand-good discover map_notes: 'the game is fully non-interactive on this candidate').
differences.expected_basis: Old-version behavior is diagnostic evidence, not an authority: the original goal ('A user can play both documented modes ... end to end') remains unmet in both candidates. F-003 stays open at high severity; not introduced by this candidate, but never resolved.

differences.delta: None at the activity level: the baseline also showed no CPU-opponent output (no CPU turn, no incoming attack) - baseline mode B was mode A's transcript plus effect markers. New in this candidate is only the D-2 consequence: the last mode-B-specific gameplay-adjacent marker (attack sound) is gone.
differences.expected_basis: README: 'Mode B (versus): player vs CPU attack mode.' CPU absence fails the original goal in both candidates; F-004 stays open at high severity.

verified_unchanged.check: Mode A full transcript byte-equivalent (decoded text) to baseline mode-a-run1.txt: same 10 lines, lock+clear sound markers present, score 1200, exit 0.

--help output present and identical to baseline probe-help.txt (usage line, -h/--help, --mode {a,b}, --smoke; exit 0). This surface was probed in the baseline but not in cand-bad discover; compare confirms it did not disappear.
--mode b --smoke combination still prints SMOKE-OK and exits 0, identical to baseline probe-modeb-smoke.txt. Also not probed in cand-bad discover; confirmed not disappeared.
Session end-state unchanged in both modes: 'game over: score 1200', exit code 0, no crashes, tracebacks, or hangs on any probed path.

goal_reconciliation.mode_a: Ends to end (exit 0) and matches README's lock/clear SFX claims, but the goal's 'user can play' is unmet (D-4/F-003, non-interactive) and an undocumented attack step exists (D-3/F-001). Same state as baseline; no regression, no repair.
goal_reconciliation.mode_b: Ends to end (exit 0) but now violates README SFX claims that the previous candidate satisfied (D-1/D-2 regression on top of F-002); 'player vs CPU' remains unmet (D-5/F-004). Mode B is the surface actively damaged in this candidate.
goal_reconciliation.overall: Original goal not met on this candidate. Blocking items: F-002 (high, regression per D-1/D-2), F-003 (high, known-old), F-004 (high, known-old). Non-blocking open item: F-001 (medium, known-old).

findings_note: No new findings added in compare. F-002's classification is upgraded by this phase from 'defect' to 'confirmed regression' (see D-1/D-2); F-001/F-003/F-004 are classified known-old-issue re baseline (D-3/D-4/D-5). All remain status confirmed and keep their severities; known-old-issue never dismisses critical/high findings per finding rules.

capability_gaps.detail: stdout-only backend: actual audibility of SFX is not capturable by the observer in either round; sound verification relies on the product's own [sound:...] markers. The regression in D-1 is proven at the marker/log channel; physical audio behavior remains unverifiable here.
The screen-shake flash itself is not capturable through stdout; only the [fx:screen-shake] marker is observable (present in mode B in both candidates).

lease.note: sequential single-runner use; no other UI runners active during the window

notes: Compare executed per packet: inputs limited to original goal, cand-bad discover result (hash-verified), baseline cand-good discover evidence, unchanged README, plus live diagnostic probes of the candidate (fresh mode A/mode B runs, --help, --mode b --smoke). No source code, diffs, tests, or prior review results were read. Old-version behavior treated as diagnostic evidence only, never as authority. Phase finished; overall acceptance conclusion is not declared by this result.
